sources.citation: Gerstner-Link, Claudia. 2026. Clans, spirits, land and food: Kilmeri texts (Open Text Collections 7). Berlin: Language Science Press. doi:10.5281/zenodo.17702074 (open access).
sources.note: Sec. 5.2 'Phonology' (pp. 42-44) gives vowel/consonant inventories, biphonemic vowel sequences, CV/CVC syllable structure, orthography and morphophonemics; it says nothing about where word stress falls. Only incidental mention p. 291 (song text B.13): 'Stressed vowels at the end of a word sound like a rising diphthong' - presupposes stress but states no rule. Refers readers to Gerstner-Link 2018 for phonology.

sources.citation: Gerstner-Link, Claudia. 2023. Multilateral lexical transfer among four Papuan language families: Border, Nimboran, Sentani, and Sko. In M. Klamer & F. R. Moro (eds.), Traces of Contact in the Lexicon: Austronesian and Papuan Studies, 263-306. Leiden: Brill (open access via OAPEN). doi:10.1163/9789004529458_009.
sources.note: No stress rule. Kilmeri forms are cited in IPA with an acute marking stress, and stress position varies across items: p. 274 'The Kilmeri form is básɪp' (initial); p. 275 Kilmeri imalɔ and Nimboran imúo 'share the second-syllable stress'; p. 276 Kilmeri sájɔ vs Nimboran sáia 'the stress pattern is the same'. Suggests stress is not uniformly fixed, but the author states no generalisation here.
sources.venue: Traces of Contact in the Lexicon: Austronesian and Papuan Studies

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Kilmeri language' (sourced from Gerstner-Link 2018 and Foley 2018).
sources.note: Gives consonant and 8-vowel inventory and 'main syllable structure is CV'; does not mention stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: SIL International, Language & Culture Archives resource list for Kilmeri [kih] (Internet Archive copy 2016-04-02) and archive item 23659 page (2024-08-10).
sources.note: Listing shows exactly one SIL item for Kilmeri (Brown 1981); no Organised Phonology Data or other phonological description exists in the SIL archive for this language.

sources.note: Nothing: sociolinguistic survey only (villages, populations, language use, cognate percentages, E/W dialects ~80% cognate, allocation sites). No phonology, no stress.

The DSpace record tags dc.language kih/kilm1241 and subject 'Kilmeri language', but the original reel label reads 'Kilinani [?]' (Glottolog knows no languoid of that name), so the Kilmeri identity is the cataloguer's reading.
